papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Emulsion, Cutting Oil, and Synthetic Oil-Free Fluids on Machining Temperatures and Performance in Side Milling of Ti-6Al-4V
papers.abstract: During machining, most of the mechanical energy is converted into heat. A substantial part of this heat is transferred to the cutting tool, causing a rapid rise in tool temperature. Excessive thermal loads accelerate tool wear and lead to displacement of the tool center point, reducing machining accuracy and workpiece quality. This challenge is particularly pronounced when machining titanium alloys. Due to their low thermal conductivity, titanium alloys impose significantly higher thermal loads on the cutting tool compared to conventional carbon steels, making the process more difficult. To reduce temperatures in the cutting zone, cutting fluids are widely employed in titanium machining. They have been shown to significantly extend tool life. Cutting fluids are broadly categorized into cutting oils and water-based cutting fluids. Owing to their distinct thermophysical properties, these fluids exhibit notably different cooling and lubrication performance. However, current research lacks comprehensive cross-comparative studies of different cutting fluid types, which hinders the selection of optimal cutting fluids for process optimization. This study examines the influence of three cutting fluids—emulsion, cutting oil, and synthetic oil-free fluid—on tool wear, temperature, surface quality, and energy consumption during flood-cooled end milling of Ti-6Al-4V. A novel experimental setup incorporating embedded thermocouples enabled real-time temperature measurement near the cutting edge. Tool wear, torque, and surface roughness were recorded over defined feed lengths. Among the tested fluids, emulsion achieved the best balance of cooling and lubrication, resulting in the longest tool life with a feed travel path of 12.21 m. This corresponds to an increase of approximately 200% compared to cutting oil and oil-free fluid. Cutting oil offered superior lubrication but limited cooling capacity, resulting in localized thermal damage and edge chipping. Water-based cutting fluids reduced tool temperatures by over 300 °C compared to dry cutting but, in some cases, increased notch wear due to higher mechanical stress at the entry point. Power consumption analysis revealed that the cutting fluid supply system accounted for 60–70% of total energy use, particularly with high-viscosity fluids like cutting oil. Complementary thermal and CFD simulations were used to quantify heat partitioning and convective cooling efficiency. The results showed that water-based fluids achieved heat transfer coefficients up to 175 kW/m2·K, more than ten times higher than those of cutting oil. These findings emphasize the importance of selecting suitable cutting fluids and optimizing their supply to enhance tool performance and energy efficiency in Ti-6Al-4V machining.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究传统铣削中冷却液对Ti-6Al-4V加工性能的影响，不涉及增材制造或后处理，与本方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: paper does not involve additive manufacturing or post-processing of AM Ti-6Al-4V; it focuses on cutting fluid performance in conventional milling of Ti-6Al-4V.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究不同切削液对钛合金铣削温度和性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 通过嵌入式热电偶实时测量切削区温度，结合CFD仿真分析。
summary_zh.result: 乳化液在冷却和润滑间取得最佳平衡，刀具寿命延长约200%。
summary_zh.validation: 实验测量与仿真结果对比验证。

summary_en.motivation: To compare the effects of different cutting fluids on machining temperatures and performance in side milling of Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: Real-time temperature measurement near the cutting edge using embedded thermocouples, complemented by thermal and CFD simulations.
summary_en.result: Emulsion achieved the best balance of cooling and lubrication, increasing tool life by approximately 200% compared to cutting oil and oil-free fluid.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements were validated against CFD simulations and heat transfer coefficient calculations.

papers.title: Influence of deflected abrasive waterjet process on surface integrity and fretting fatigue properties of Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy dovetails
papers.abstract: Water jet peening holds great promise for enhancing the surface integrity and fatigue properties of materials. The deflected abrasive waterjet peening (DAWJP) process is well-suited for surface peening of metal components with confined geometries. Pressure is a key parameter that affects the surface strengthening of material. In this research, the dovetail slot of Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy was strengthened using the DAWJP developed by our research group. The surface integrity of the dovetail slots before and after treatment under DAWJP processes at three pressures was systematically investigated, covering aspects such as surface roughness, residual stresses, microhardness, and microscopic morphology. The results indicated that under the DAWJP process with pressures of 50 MPa, 100 MPa, and 150 MPa, the depth of the plastic layer reached 18 μm, 23 μm, and 28 μm respectively. After DAWJP treatment, the surface roughness of the specimens was in 2 the range of 0.325 - 0.376 μm, and the microhardness was between 477.57 - 575.93 HV, showing an improvement compared to the original specimens. The maximum residual stresses at the three pressures occurred at depths of 17 μm, 20 μm, and 26 μm, with maximum values of - 642.41 MPa, - 692.62 MPa, and - 729.62 MPa respectively. At a load of 6 KN, the fretting fatigue life of the strengthened dovetail is 5.91 times and 2.15 times that of the unstrengthened one at room temperature and 400 °C respectively. The overall findings demonstrate that the employed DAWJP process can remarkably improve the fretting fatigue life of dovetail slots, with a particularly significant effect at room temperature.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了喷丸后处理对Ti-6Al-4V钛合金表面完整性和微动疲劳性能的影响，虽未涉及增材制造，但后处理方法和结果对增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理控制具有参考价值。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not specify that the Ti-6Al-4V material is additively manufactured (AM), so its direct applicability to AM Ti-6Al-4V post-processing control is limited; it focuses on conventionally manufactured dovetails.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索偏转磨料水射流喷丸工艺对Ti-6Al-4V榫槽表面完整性及微动疲劳寿命的提升效果。
summary_zh.method: 在不同压力下对Ti-6Al-4V榫槽进行偏转磨料水射流喷丸处理，测试表面粗糙度、残余应力、显微硬度及微动疲劳寿命。
summary_zh.result: 150 MPa压力下塑性层深度28 μm，最大残余应力-729.62 MPa，室温下疲劳寿命提升至原始试样的5.91倍。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验对比处理前后表面完整性及标准微动疲劳测试验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the potential of deflected abrasive waterjet peening (DAWJP) in improving surface integrity and fretting fatigue life of Ti-6Al-4V dovetail slots.
summary_en.method: DAWJP was applied at three pressures (50, 100, 150 MPa) to Ti-6Al-4V dovetails, and surface roughness, residual stress, microhardness, and fretting fatigue life were characterized.
summary_en.result: DAWJP treatment increased plastic layer depth up to 28 μm, maximum compressive residual stress up to -729.62 MPa, and fretting fatigue life at room temperature by 5.91 times compared to untreated specimens.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements of surface integrity and standard fretting fatigue tests were conducted to validate the effect of DAWJP.
